ADVISOR RULING (02:30), guard channel: APPROVE the named FIFO outside every writable root, in a read-only-bound dir, read by aida (replaces the inherited fd). FAIL CLOSED: if a guard can't write its event, it exits nonzero WITHOUT exec'ing the tool, so a lost event can never coexist with a successful tool call. aida treats any guard exit code 98 or an EOF anomaly as not clean. Keep your probe as a test: the default Python subprocess.run(capture_output=True) case records the hit.

ADVISOR RULING (02:30), adapter scope, amending my TASK-1732 signoff: identifier validation isn't enough. TARGETS (the env names the adapter sets) must NOT be in the protected set: PATH, HOME, SHELL, ENV, BASH_ENV, IFS, TMPDIR, PWD, OLDPWD, and any name with the prefixes LD_, DYLD_, PYTHON, PERL, RUBY, NODE_, JAVA_, CLASSPATH, GIT_, XDG_, AIDA_, LC_ (LANG too), plus any variable the scorer itself sets for the oracle. SOURCES may not be AIDA_* internals or protected names. A violation is a hard error naming the mapping. Mapped VALUES are copied verbatim from the source variable; never path-expanded. Test: a mapping AIDA_REGEN_TRIAL_ROOT->PATH (and ->PYTHONPATH) is refused.
subject: RULINGS: guard FIFO (fail closed) + adapter protected targets
